title: Topos Institute Research Bridge

hero.headline: Reduce the new machinery to established formalism first.
hero.support: This unlisted brief proposes a simple test: represent one Boundary First object using the strongest relevant existing categorical or formal machinery, identify exact equivalences, and keep only the residue that genuinely survives.

bflSide: Schemathematics as an operational study of formal structures across schemas.

candidateExperiment.title: Reduction before invention
steps: Select one Schemathematics object or Boundary First invariant contract.
Represent it using the strongest relevant established categorical machinery.
Measure whether any claimed residual defect remains after the translation.
Retire the Boundary First primitive if the mature formalism already carries the necessary structure.
candidateExperiment.successCondition: A useful result includes clean reduction. The collaboration is successful if it tells us what not to invent.

firstAsk: Take one proposed Boundary First object and try to reduce it to established category-theoretic or compositional systems language. If nothing essential remains, that is a successful result.
claimBoundary: This page does not imply Topos Institute endorsement, partnership, affiliation, or review.
Schemathematics is a research program with an active novelty burden, not a declared replacement for category theory or existing formal methods.
Categorical Turing Machines and related compositional computation work remain open research directions.
Any claim of novelty must follow documented attempted reduction against established mathematics.
